name: Duck 1
what_changed: The brain is built left/right symmetric (the NET method of Abdolhosseini and others 2019): one network reads the situation and its mirror image, and the left leg commands of the mirrored view drive the right leg. The judge (critic) and the sense scaling are symmetric too, and each left/right motor pair shares one wobble.
why: The best plain brain (night run 1, 4M steps: exam 905, no falls) hopped with the right leg always leading and used the left leg as a passive prop. Francisco wants two legged walking to appear by itself, without a rhythm clock or copied motion, so symmetry is built into the brain instead of rewarded with an extra tuned number.
starts_from: zero (a new brain; no plain brain was converted)

runs.outcome: first start, stopped after two minutes; not used

planned as a 1M pilot, then continued to 2M and 6M. Alternating steps with real knee bends appeared by 1.6M. Exam best at 1.61M (484, 7 falls of 12), then a collapse: 12 of 12 falls from 4.25M on, 22 points at 6M

rerun from 1.61M with the new exam and PPO stats. Exam swung between 164 and 439. Each brain update was 50 to 100 times bigger than PPO is designed for (approx_kl 0.5 to 1.1, safety limit hit by 83 to 87% of moves), growing as the wobble shrank. Likely cause of the collapse: a fixed step size

notes: Walks with alternating steps, one foot down about 88% of the time. Passes the walking test at 0.4 m/s (8 of 10), but is fragile at other speeds: 7 of 12 exam attempts (random target speeds) end in a fall. Uses about twice the energy per metre of the plain hopper. Knee swing about 65 degrees, foot lift 6 to 7 cm. Code version: training ran on c32d242; the recipe above was read at 43acb18, which only adds the exam and stats (no change to how the duck learns).
